title: Taping the Ellington special: Eubie Blake, a marathon night and a sick Duke
summary: Eubie came but Willie the Lion was too ill; the taping ran past 3 a.m., with Ellington sick in hospital and retaped.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I just didn't know it, because we had a thing where we wanted Eubie Blake and Willie the Lion Smith, and let me see, who else -- Eubie's still the only one living, but we wanted to get a conversation in retrospect, in the old time, the James P. Johnson days, you know.
Uh-huh.

And somehow or another it just didn't work, you know. But Eubie came out and he was respected monetarily and professionally, you know. And Willie the Lion was sick. His health was failing at that point, you know.
Yeah.
So consequently, you know, he couldn't make that trip.
This was in January of 1973, right?
Was that when it was?
As I recall it was, yeah. When we taped the show, it was what, the world's longest television taping. It went to 3:00 o'clock in the morning.
Well, it was done like a movie.
Yeah.
That's what it -- you know, that's what
it meant to do. See, when I saw it at Bob Ud koff's (PHONETIC) house, and after all of the editing, it just goes down smooth.
Yeah, but it was interminable. Started out with a packed house at the Shubert Theater, and by 1:00 o'clock there was maybe a tenth of the people left.
Yeah, half a house at least.
Yeah.
So, I think they expected that, because they had gotten the usage out of the audience.
Yeah, a black tie audience.
Not only that, the faces. There were a lot of important people there, in television.
Uh-huh. Yes, there were.
And they had gotten all of that. So consequently, you know, they got what they wanted.
Uh-huh.

It didn't make any difference whether anybody walked out or not. So then when they started making the editing situation, putting that together, and you'd look at the show straight down, it doesn't offend you. But it was a very nervous situation that night.
Yeah, I remember you telling me some backstage stories. I was backstage very briefly and then I fled back out front.
Oh, yeah, well there's always tension.
You go in the truck where they have six or seven cameras going at the same -- oh, six or seven, not cameras, but --
Tape machines, right?

Tape machines coming back at you at once, and the guys are nervous and they're trying to get the thing together because it's got to be done then. There's no -- there's no repeat. And Ellington was sick at that time.
Yeah, he had pneumonia.
Yes. And he went to the hospital and came back and retaped.
Yeah.
Looked like a completely different man, you know?
He looked green. When he came out to do his part --
Yeah.
-- at the first taping? I mean his skin actually looked a greenish color.
Yeah.
He was so sick.
